title: Make sure runners auto detect models from existing harnesses Recent focus has been on muse code compatibility but we need to extend it to all supported harnesses to have aut detect and import. For example server2 locally has pi configured, we need tobe able to use those models this includes the tying it into the refresh button into the ui
goal:
# Make sure runners auto detect models from existing harnesses

Recent focus has been on muse code compatibility but we need to extend it to all supported harnesses to have aut detect and import. For example server2 locally has pi configured, we need tobe able to use those models

this includes the tying it into the refresh button into the ui

## Human Correction / Feedback
![image.png](assets/image.png)

This seems to have been failing to detect models on server 2 despite a manual update to the latestversion

# Implementation Plan — Runner auto-detect models from all supported harnesses

## Goal

Every Runner auto-detects the models of each harness it serves (not just
`muse`), advertises them to the backend through the existing heartbeat,
and the existing UI Refresh / Re-detect controls drive a fresh scan.
Concrete target: a host like server2 with `pi` configured must serve its
pi models into the fleet picker with no hand-typed model list.

## Context and evidence

- Runner discovery today is muse-only: `discoverClaudeModels()` in
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`muse serve` → `model/list`), and
  `refreshDiscoveredModels()` in `runner/daemon.js` returns early unless
  `muse` is in the configured harness list.
- The Runner bundle ships `runner/` + `api/` + `shared/` (see `deploy.sh`
  staging) and `startRunner.sh` runs `npm ci --prefix runner/api`, so the
  Runner host HAS the backend harness modules and their deps (including
  the pi SDK `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`). `defaultLoadHarness()`
  already imports backend harness factories on the Runner.
- Backend per-harness discovery already exists and is the behavior to
  reuse, not reimplement:
  - `pi`: `piHarness.listModels()` from `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()`
    (only providers with VALID credentials appear — matches survey q2).
  - `antigravity`: `agyModelCatalog.js` (`agy models` spawn + parse, TTL
    cache, classified `{code,message,hint}` errors).
  - `opencode`: `OpencodeModelDiscovery.js` (`/config/providers` fetch).
  - `muse`: MSP `model/list` (`museMspModelCatalog.js`; Runner leg exists).
  - `vibe`: ACP handshake model select (`vibeModelCatalog.js`); exec path
    honestly empty.
  - `codex`: theoretical shim, honestly empty (`listModels()` → `[]`).
  - `custom`/`mock`: no discovery (`none`, or test-only).
- Refresh plumbing already exists end to end and only needs generalizing:
  `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` "Re-detect models" →
  `api.requestModelRediscovery(runnerId)` → `RUNNER_COMMANDS` heartbeat
  pull channel (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, ADR 0013) →
  `handlePendingCommands()` → `refreshDiscoveredModels()` → ack
  `discovered N model(s)` → next heartbeat `facts.models` → fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog`) → picker fleet badges
  (`withFleetModels`, `fleetCountBadgeNode`).
- Precedence already implemented: explicit `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS/MODEL`
  wins over discovery (`resolveAdvertisedModels`, pinned check in
  `handlePendingCommands`). Empty-scan behavior already implemented for
  muse: failures keep the previous cache and warn.
- `SURVEY.md` in this task folder is UNANSWERED (empty `answers: {}`),
  and the `idea-*.md` report named in the stage brief is not on disk.
  This plan adopts the survey's Recommended options as assumptions
  (flagged ASSUMPTION below) so the first implementation pass is
  reviewable without blocking on the survey.

## Survey assumptions (all from SURVEY.md Recommended options)

- ASSUMPTION q1 (scope): all six named harnesses — pi, muse, codex,
  opencode, vibe, antigravity. Codex/opencode legs are honest-empty until
  runnable (see Phase 0 spikes); this matches the backend honesty rule
  (never serve models that cannot run there).
- ASSUMPTION q2 (what to list): only models ready to use right now
  (logged in / valid credentials). This is what the reused
  `listModels()` legs already yield.
- ASSUMPTION q3 (Refresh button): ask the Runner to scan again right away
  and update the list. This is the existing `requestModelRediscovery`
  command; keep it, generalize the scan.
- ASSUMPTION q4 (precedence): the typed-in list wins, auto-detect ignored.
  Already implemented; keep and extend tests.
- ASSUMPTION q5 (empty scan): keep the old list, show a small warning.
  Already implemented for muse; generalize per-harness slices + status.
- ASSUMPTION q6 (presentation): detected models appear as normal choices
  in the model picker (fleet-joined options), not a separate Pi section.
  Already how `withFleetModels` works; no picker redesign.

## Approach (make change easy, then make the change)

Do NOT add five more one-off `discoverXModels` functions beside
`discoverClaudeModels`. Instead:

1. First (Phase 1) extract a Runner-side **discovery registry**:
   `harnessId → async discover(ctx) → string[]` with one shared cache,
   shared timeout/best-effort wrapper, and shared fleet-id mapping —
   migrating the muse leg into it with ZERO behavior change.
2. Then (Phase 2) add one leg per harness behind the same contract,
   each reusing the backend harness's own `listModels()` (single source
   of truth for "ready to use"), with fixture-seamed unit tests.
3. Then (Phase 3) wire status/UX: per-harness counts and first-error in
   the command ack + heartbeat facts, surfaced by the existing Runner
   detail status line. No new screens.

## Steps

### Phase 0 — Research spikes (first, de-risks everything)

- [ ] 0.1 Pi-on-Runner probe (server2). On a Runner host with pi
  configured (`~/.pi/agent/` holds `auth.json`, `models.json`,
  `models-store.json` on server2): import the bundled
  `api/agent/harnesses/pi/piHarness.js`, call
  `createPiHarness({}).listModels({refresh:true})`, and record: works
  headless, wall time, ids returned, behavior with no login (expect
  honest empty, no throw). Decides whether the pi leg is a direct
  `listModels()` call (expected) or needs a CLI/config-file fallback.
- [ ] 0.2 Opencode-on-Runner feasibility. Determine what an opencode leg
  would talk to on a Runner host: existing `OPENCODE_URL` vs spawning
  `opencode serve` per discovery round (cost, port, lifecycle). If neither
  is sane, scope opencode to honest-empty + status
  (`opencode server not reachable`) and note the follow-up.
- [ ] 0.3 Codex transport check. Confirm the live `codex` model-listing
  surface is still UNVERIFIED (see `codexHarness.js` header). Expected
  outcome: no codex leg this round; shim stays honest-empty. Record the
  decision in the plan file before Phase 2 starts.
- [ ] 0.4 Dispatch-match verification. Read
  `api/flow/dispatch/taskRequirements.js` + `runnerMatches.js` and confirm
  a fleet-advertised id (e.g. `pi::google::gemini-x`) dispatched from a
  picker exactly matches that Runner (the "fleet pick is a guaranteed
  match" invariant). Record any grammar fix needed before legs land.
- [ ] 0.5 Fleet-counts freshness check. Confirm how `/runners/models`
  catalogue readers refresh after a re-detection (poll vs manual
  reload), so Phase 3 knows whether the picker needs a refresh nudge or
  docs-only guidance. Record outcome.

### Phase 1 — Make change easy: discovery registry + muse migration (no behavior change)

- [ ] 1.1 Add `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`: `DISCOVERY_LEGS`
  registry (`{ [harnessId]: async (ctx) => string[] }`), `discoverModelsForHarnesses(ids, ctx)`
  (per-leg timeout, best-effort, dedupe, fleet-id grammar validation
  `harness::provider::id`, colon rejection like today), per-harness
  cache slices (`{ ids, atMs, error }`). Reuse `withModelKey` from
  `api/models.js` for id mapping so Runner ids are byte-identical to
  backend keys.
- [ ] 1.2 Migrate the muse leg into the registry as `muse:
  discoverClaudeModels` wrapper. Keep `discoverClaudeModels` export
  (tests + compat). No new harnesses yet.
- [ ] 1.3 Rework `refreshDiscoveredModels()` to iterate
  `runnerHarnessIds(config)` through the registry instead of the
  muse-only early return. Keep: pinned-models early return, keep-old-on-
  failure (now per-harness slice), warn-never-throw, log line (now with
  per-harness counts, e.g. `pi:12 muse:3`).
- [ ] 1.4 Rework the `requestModelRediscovery` ack detail to
  `discovered N model(s) (pi:12, muse:3)` and include the first leg
  error code when a leg fails (still `ok:true`, cache kept).
- [ ] 1.5 Unit tests: registry contract (timeout → `[]`, throw → `[]`,
  dedupe, grammar validation, per-slice keep-old), muse migration
  parity (existing `modelDiscovery.test.js` + `daemon.test.js` cases
  still pass unmodified where possible), ack detail format. New
  `runner/*.test.js` files must be registered in the explicit file list
  in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` ("Unit Tests (runner)" suite) or they never
  run.
- [ ] 1.6 Gate: `npm test` (the root gate runs the api, frontend, AND
  runner suites; `npm run test:unit` alone skips the runner suite) +
  `npm run lint` green.

### Phase 2 — Make the change: one leg per harness

Order by value and certainty (pi first — the task's concrete need).

- [ ] 2.1 `pi` leg: dynamic import the bundled pi harness factory,
  `listModels({refresh:true})`, map to `key` ids. Seams: injectable
  harness factory + listModels for fixture tests. Timeout ~20s.
  Do NOT read keys; the SDK snapshot already encodes credential validity.
- [ ] 2.2 `antigravity` leg: reuse `createAgyModelCatalog` with a
  `refresh`-equivalent (its `clearCache()` + `listAgyModels()`), map to
  keys. Reuse its classified errors for the leg error slot.
- [ ] 2.3 `vibe` leg: reuse `createVibeModelCatalog().listModels()`
  (handshake-only probe, no prompt, no cost). Exec-only hosts yield
  honest empty + retained error.
- [ ] 2.4 `muse` leg: already done in Phase 1 (keep as the reference
  implementation for leg shape).
- [ ] 2.5 `opencode` + `codex` legs: per Phase 0 outcomes — expected
  honest-empty legs returning `[]` with a status reason (no fake ids).
  If 0.2 finds a sane opencode path, implement it the same way
  (server URL from env, short fetch timeout).
- [ ] 2.6 `custom`/`mock`: explicitly NO legs (documented non-goal;
  `mock` never auto-detects, `custom` manages its own model).
- [ ] 2.7 AUTO_DETECTABLE_HARNESSES review: `pi,muse,antigravity,vibe`
  already covered; add `codex`/`opencode` to PATH auto-detect ONLY if
  `defaultLoadHarness` can run them (today it cannot) — otherwise leave
  detection as-is and record why. Do not expand runnable scope by
  accident.
- [ ] 2.8 Tests per leg: fixture-driven (fake harness/catalogue, no
  CLIs): happy path ids, empty login → `[]` + status, throw/timeout →
  `[]` + status, colon/malformed ids skipped, cross-leg dedupe.
- [ ] 2.9 Gate: `npm test` green (covers the runner suite).

### Phase 3 — Refresh-button + status UX (tie-in)

- [ ] 3.1 Heartbeat facts: add additive `facts.discoveryStatus`
  (`{ [harnessId]: { ok, count, atMs, error?: {code,message} } }`).
  Backend ignores unknown fields (additive, old backends safe).
- [ ] 3.2 Backend: persist `discoveryStatus` from facts into the runner
  record capabilities projection (same path as `facts.models`), serve
  it on the runner rows API. No schema break: absent = unknown, never
  mislead.
- [ ] 3.3 Frontend `RunnerConfigurationSection`: extend the existing
  re-detect status line to show per-harness counts from the ack detail
  (already rendered) and, when present, the first leg warning. Keep-old
  list behavior: no list change on failure (already true). No new
  buttons: the existing "Re-detect models" IS the refresh button for
  this screen (survey q3).
- [ ] 3.4 `ModelSelector` empty-state Refresh (`onRefresh` →
  `/compute/models?refresh=true`) already covers backend-host
  catalogues; verify it needs no change for fleet-joined options and
  record the outcome (Phase 0.5 input). Expected: docs-only.
- [ ] 3.5 Frontend tests: status-line renders counts + warning, empty
  list keeps old rows on failed re-detection, no-`discoveryStatus`
  (old backend) renders as today.
- [ ] 3.6 Headless verification only (per stage guidance): use existing
  mock fixtures + `npm run capture:screenshot` for the Runner models
  block and picker empty state. No long-lived dev servers.
- [ ] 3.7 Gate: `npm run test:frontend` + `npm run lint:frontend` green.

### Phase 4 — Assurance: E2E, docs, rollout

- [ ] 4.1 E2E on server2 (real pi): boot/point a Runner with
  pi auto-detect, no pinned models; assert heartbeat advertises
  `pi::…` ids; press Re-detect; assert ack counts + fleet picker shows
  the models as normal choices; revoke login (or stop agent) and assert
  keep-old + warning. Record commands + output in the task folder.
- [ ] 4.2 Regression: pinned-models Runner still skips discovery with
  the "models pinned" ack; muse-only Runner output byte-identical to
  before (Phase 1 parity).
- [ ] 4.3 Docs: update `docs/EngineDetails/HarnessModelSelector.md`
  (runner legs matrix), `runner/README.md` (env knobs unchanged +
  per-harness behavior), `api/agent/harnesses/README.md` (runner
  discovery column if it has a matrix), `CHANGELOG.md` entry.
  Keep `SURVEY.md` untouched (survey record).
- [ ] 4.4 Full gate: `npm test`, `npm run lint`,
  `npm run docs:check` green.

## Validation plan (maps to phases)

| Phase | Check | Expected evidence |
| 0 | probe scripts on server2 | notes in task folder: pi ids, timings, login-absent behavior |
| 1 | `npm test`, `lint` | green; muse parity tests pass |
| 2 | `npm test` | green; per-leg fixture tests pass |
| 3 | `npm run test:frontend`, `capture:screenshot` | green; screenshots of status line + empty state |
| 4 | server2 E2E + `docs:check` | recorded transcript; docs gate green |

## Risks and mitigations

## Goal

Every Runner auto-detects the models of each harness it serves (not just
`muse`), advertises them to the backend through the existing heartbeat,
and the existing UI Refresh / Re-detect controls drive a fresh scan.

pi models into the fleet picker with no hand-typed model list.

## Context and evidence

- Runner discovery today is muse-only: `discoverClaudeModels()` in
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`muse serve` → `model/list`), and
  `refreshDiscoveredModels()` in `runner/daemon.js` returns early unless
  `muse` is in the configured harness list.
- The Runner bundle ships `runner/` + `api/` + `shared/` (see `deploy.sh`
  staging) and `startRunner.sh` runs `npm ci --prefix runner/api`, so the
  Runner host HAS the backend harness modules and their deps (including
  the pi SDK `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`). `defaultLoadHarness()`
  already imports backend harness factories on the Runner.
- Backend per-harness discovery already exists and is the behavior to
  reuse, not reimplement:
  - `pi`: `piHarness.listModels()` from `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()`
    (only providers with VALID credentials appear — matches survey q2).
  - `antigravity`: `agyModelCatalog.js` (`agy models` spawn + parse, TTL
    cache, classified `{code,message,hint}` errors).
  - `opencode`: `OpencodeModelDiscovery.js` (`/config/providers` fetch).
  - `muse`: MSP `model/list` (`museMspModelCatalog.js`; Runner leg exists).
  - `vibe`: ACP handshake model select (`vibeModelCatalog.js`); exec path
    honestly empty.
  - `codex`: theoretical shim, honestly empty (`listModels()` → `[]`).
  - `custom`/`mock`: no discovery (`none`, or test-only).
- Refresh plumbing already exists end to end and only needs generalizing:
  `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` "Re-detect models" →
  `api.requestModelRediscovery(runnerId)` → `RUNNER_COMMANDS` heartbeat
  pull channel (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, ADR 0013) →
  `handlePendingCommands()` → `refreshDiscoveredModels()` → ack
  `discovered N model(s)` → next heartbeat `facts.models` → fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog`) → picker fleet badges
  (`withFleetModels`, `fleetCountBadgeNode`).
- Precedence already implemented: explicit `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS/MODEL`
  wins over discovery (`resolveAdvertisedModels`, pinned check in
  `handlePendingCommands`). Empty-scan behavior already implemented for
  muse: failures keep the previous cache and warn.
- `SURVEY.md` in this task folder is UNANSWERED (empty `answers: {}`),
  and the `idea-*.md` report named in the stage brief is not on disk.
  This plan adopts the survey's Recommended options as assumptions
  (flagged ASSUMPTION below) so the first implementation pass is
  reviewable without blocking on the survey.

## Survey assumptions (all from SURVEY.md Recommended options)

- ASSUMPTION q1 (scope): all six named harnesses — pi, muse, codex,
  opencode, vibe, antigravity. Codex/opencode legs are honest-empty until
  runnable (see Phase 0 spikes); this matches the backend honesty rule
  (never serve models that cannot run there).
- ASSUMPTION q2 (what to list): only models ready to use right now
  (logged in / valid credentials). This is what the reused
  `listModels()` legs already yield.
- ASSUMPTION q3 (Refresh button): ask the Runner to scan again right away
  and update the list. This is the existing `requestModelRediscovery`
  command; keep it, generalize the scan.
- ASSUMPTION q4 (precedence): the typed-in list wins, auto-detect ignored.

  catalogue readers refresh after a re-detection (poll vs manual
  reload), so Phase 3 knows whether the picker needs a refresh nudge or

  backend keys.
- [ ] 1.2 Migrate the muse leg into the registry as `muse:
  discoverClaudeModels` wrapper. Keep `discoverClaudeModels` export
  (tests + compat). No new harnesses yet.
- [ ] 1.3 Rework `refreshDiscoveredModels()` to iterate
  `runnerHarnessIds(config)` through the registry instead of the
  muse-only early return. Keep: pinned-models early return, keep-old-on-

  per-harness counts, e.g. `pi:12 muse:3`).

  parity (existing `modelDiscovery.test.js` + `daemon.test.js` cases

### Phase 2 — Make the change: one leg per harness

Order by value and certainty (pi first — the task's concrete need).

- [ ] 2.1 `pi` leg: dynamic import the bundled pi harness factory,
  `listModels({refresh:true})`, map to `key` ids. Seams: injectable
  harness factory + listModels for fixture tests. Timeout ~20s.

# Implementation Plan — Runner auto-detect models from all supported harnesses

## Goal

Every Runner auto-detects the models of each harness it serves (not just
`muse`), advertises them to the backend through the existing heartbeat,
and the existing UI Refresh / Re-detect controls drive a fresh scan.
Concrete target: a host like server2 with `pi` configured must serve its
pi models into the fleet picker with no hand-typed model list.

## Context and evidence

- Runner discovery today is muse-only: `discoverClaudeModels()` in
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`muse serve` → `model/list`), and
  `refreshDiscoveredModels()` in `runner/daemon.js` returns early unless
  `muse` is in the configured harness list.
- The Runner bundle ships `runner/` + `api/` + `shared/` (see `deploy.sh`
  staging) and `startRunner.sh` runs `npm ci --prefix runner/api`, so the
  Runner host HAS the backend harness modules and their deps (including
  the pi SDK `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`). `defaultLoadHarness()`
  already imports backend harness factories on the Runner.
- Backend per-harness discovery already exists and is the behavior to
  reuse, not reimplement:
  - `pi`: `piHarness.listModels()` from `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()`
    (only providers with VALID credentials appear — matches survey q2).
  - `antigravity`: `agyModelCatalog.js` (`agy models` spawn + parse, TTL
    cache, classified `{code,message,hint}` errors).
  - `opencode`: `OpencodeModelDiscovery.js` (`/config/providers` fetch).
  - `muse`: MSP `model/list` (`museMspModelCatalog.js`; Runner leg exists).
  - `vibe`: ACP handshake model select (`vibeModelCatalog.js`); exec path
    honestly empty.
  - `codex`: theoretical shim, honestly empty (`listModels()` → `[]`).
  - `custom`/`mock`: no discovery (`none`, or test-only).
- Refresh plumbing already exists end to end and only needs generalizing:
  `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` "Re-detect models" →
  `api.requestModelRediscovery(runnerId)` → `RUNNER_COMMANDS` heartbeat
  pull channel (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, ADR 0013) →
  `handlePendingCommands()` → `refreshDiscoveredModels()` → ack
  `discovered N model(s)` → next heartbeat `facts.models` → fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog`) → picker fleet badges
  (`withFleetModels`, `fleetCountBadgeNode`).
- Precedence already implemented: explicit `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS/MODEL`
  wins over discovery (`resolveAdvertisedModels`, pinned check in
  `handlePendingCommands`). Empty-scan behavior already implemented for
  muse: failures keep the previous cache and warn.
- `SURVEY.md` in this task folder is UNANSWERED (empty `answers: {}`),
  and the `idea-*.md` report named in the stage brief is not on disk.
  This plan adopts the survey's Recommended options as assumptions
  (flagged ASSUMPTION below) so the first implementation pass is
  reviewable without blocking on the survey.

## Survey assumptions (all from SURVEY.md Recommended options)

- ASSUMPTION q1 (scope): all six named harnesses — pi, muse, codex,
  opencode, vibe, antigravity. Codex/opencode legs are honest-empty until
  runnable (see Phase 0 spikes); this matches the backend honesty rule
  (never serve models that cannot run there).
- ASSUMPTION q2 (what to list): only models ready to use right now
  (logged in / valid credentials). This is what the reused
  `listModels()` legs already yield.
- ASSUMPTION q3 (Refresh button): ask the Runner to scan again right away
  and update the list. This is the existing `requestModelRediscovery`
  command; keep it, generalize the scan.
- ASSUMPTION q4 (precedence): the typed-in list wins, auto-detect ignored.
  Already implemented; keep and extend tests.
- ASSUMPTION q5 (empty scan): keep the old list, show a small warning.
  Already implemented for muse; generalize per-harness slices + status.
- ASSUMPTION q6 (presentation): detected models appear as normal choices
  in the model picker (fleet-joined options), not a separate Pi section.
  Already how `withFleetModels` works; no picker redesign.

## Approach (make change easy, then make the change)

Do NOT add five more one-off `discoverXModels` functions beside
`discoverClaudeModels`. Instead:

1. First (Phase 1) extract a Runner-side **discovery registry**:
   `harnessId → async discover(ctx) → string[]` with one shared cache,
   shared timeout/best-effort wrapper, and shared fleet-id mapping —
   migrating the muse leg into it with ZERO behavior change.
2. Then (Phase 2) add one leg per harness behind the same contract,
   each reusing the backend harness's own `listModels()` (single source
   of truth for "ready to use"), with fixture-seamed unit tests.
3. Then (Phase 3) wire status/UX: per-harness counts and first-error in
   the command ack + heartbeat facts, surfaced by the existing Runner
   detail status line. No new screens.

### Phase 0 — Research spikes (first, de-risks everything)

- [ ] 0.1 Pi-on-Runner probe (server2). On a Runner host with pi
  configured (`~/.pi/agent/` holds `auth.json`, `models.json`,
  `models-store.json` on server2): import the bundled

  cache slices (`{ ids, atMs, error }`). Reuse `withModelKey` from
  `api/models.js` for id mapping so Runner ids are byte-identical to
  backend keys.
- [ ] 1.2 Migrate the muse leg into the registry as `muse:
  discoverClaudeModels` wrapper. Keep `discoverClaudeModels` export
  (tests + compat). No new harnesses yet.
- [ ] 1.3 Rework `refreshDiscoveredModels()` to iterate
  `runnerHarnessIds(config)` through the registry instead of the
  muse-only early return. Keep: pinned-models early return, keep-old-on-
  failure (now per-harness slice), warn-never-throw, log line (now with
  per-harness counts, e.g. `pi:12 muse:3`).
- [ ] 1.4 Rework the `requestModelRediscovery` ack detail to
  `discovered N model(s) (pi:12, muse:3)` and include the first leg
  error code when a leg fails (still `ok:true`, cache kept).
- [ ] 1.5 Unit tests: registry contract (timeout → `[]`, throw → `[]`,
  dedupe, grammar validation, per-slice keep-old), muse migration
  parity (existing `modelDiscovery.test.js` + `daemon.test.js` cases
  still pass unmodified where possible), ack detail format. New
  `runner/*.test.js` files must be registered in the explicit file list
  in `scripts/run-tests.mjs` ("Unit Tests (runner)" suite) or they never
  run.
- [ ] 1.6 Gate: `npm test` (the root gate runs the api, frontend, AND
  runner suites; `npm run test:unit` alone skips the runner suite) +
  `npm run lint` green.

### Phase 2 — Make the change: one leg per harness

Order by value and certainty (pi first — the task's concrete need).

- [ ] 2.1 `pi` leg: dynamic import the bundled pi harness factory,
  `listModels({refresh:true})`, map to `key` ids. Seams: injectable
  harness factory + listModels for fixture tests. Timeout ~20s.
  Do NOT read keys; the SDK snapshot already encodes credential validity.
- [ ] 2.2 `antigravity` leg: reuse `createAgyModelCatalog` with a
  `refresh`-equivalent (its `clearCache()` + `listAgyModels()`), map to
  keys. Reuse its classified errors for the leg error slot.
- [ ] 2.3 `vibe` leg: reuse `createVibeModelCatalog().listModels()`
  (handshake-only probe, no prompt, no cost). Exec-only hosts yield
  honest empty + retained error.

- [ ] 2.7 AUTO_DETECTABLE_HARNESSES review: `pi,muse,antigravity,vibe`

  `defaultLoadHarness` can run them (today it cannot) — otherwise leave
  detection as-is and record why. Do not expand runnable scope by

# Implementation Plan — Runner auto-detect models from all supported harnesses

## Goal

Every Runner auto-detects the models of each harness it serves (not just
`muse`), advertises them to the backend through the existing heartbeat,
and the existing UI Refresh / Re-detect controls drive a fresh scan.
Concrete target: a host like server2 with `pi` configured must serve its
pi models into the fleet picker with no hand-typed model list.

## Context and evidence

- Runner discovery today is muse-only: `discoverClaudeModels()` in
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`muse serve` → `model/list`), and
  `refreshDiscoveredModels()` in `runner/daemon.js` returns early unless
  `muse` is in the configured harness list.
- The Runner bundle ships `runner/` + `api/` + `shared/` (see `deploy.sh`
  staging) and `startRunner.sh` runs `npm ci --prefix runner/api`, so the
  Runner host HAS the backend harness modules and their deps (including
  the pi SDK `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`). `defaultLoadHarness()`
  already imports backend harness factories on the Runner.
- Backend per-harness discovery already exists and is the behavior to
  reuse, not reimplement:
  - `pi`: `piHarness.listModels()` from `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()`
    (only providers with VALID credentials appear — matches survey q2).
  - `antigravity`: `agyModelCatalog.js` (`agy models` spawn + parse, TTL
    cache, classified `{code,message,hint}` errors).
  - `opencode`: `OpencodeModelDiscovery.js` (`/config/providers` fetch).
  - `muse`: MSP `model/list` (`museMspModelCatalog.js`; Runner leg exists).
  - `vibe`: ACP handshake model select (`vibeModelCatalog.js`); exec path
    honestly empty.
  - `codex`: theoretical shim, honestly empty (`listModels()` → `[]`).
  - `custom`/`mock`: no discovery (`none`, or test-only).
- Refresh plumbing already exists end to end and only needs generalizing:
  `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` "Re-detect models" →
  `api.requestModelRediscovery(runnerId)` → `RUNNER_COMMANDS` heartbeat
  pull channel (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, ADR 0013) →
  `handlePendingCommands()` → `refreshDiscoveredModels()` → ack
  `discovered N model(s)` → next heartbeat `facts.models` → fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog`) → picker fleet badges

# Phase 0 spike notes — Runner auto-detect models from all harnesses

Recorded 2026-11-10 on server2 (working dir `kb-2cbe91b6-8ccd-4e96-8929-963576b86999`).
All probes read-only; no live backend or runner touched.

## 0.1 Pi-on-Runner probe — PASS (direct `listModels()` call)

- `~/.pi/agent/` holds `auth.json`, `models.json`, `models-store.json` (pi configured, no `pi` CLI on PATH — SDK only).
- `createPiHarness({}).listModels({refresh:true})` headless: **77 models in ~960ms**, keys already canonical (`pi::mistral::codestral-2508`, via `withModelKey`).
- No-login simulation (`HOME=/tmp/empty-home-probe`): **0 models, no throw** — honest empty as expected.
- Decision: pi leg is a direct `listModels({refresh:true})` call through the bundled backend harness factory. No CLI/config-file fallback needed.

# server2 auto-detect fix — verification record (2026-11-10)

## Root cause of the human-reported failure

server2's runner env (`~/.kainbain/runner-server2-alpha.env`) pinned
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=muse`, so the daemon's harness list was
`['muse']` and the discovery round only ran the muse leg — journal showed
`Model discovery: 0 model(s) (muse:0)` on every Re-detect, even with the
latest runner code deployed. On top of that, the Runner's harness
auto-detect probed only PATH, and server2's systemd PATH
(`/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`) does not include
`~/.local/bin` or `~/.pi/agent/bin`, so even `auto` would have missed pi
(the backend's own `discoverHarnesses` detects pi via the
`~/.pi/agent/models.json` snapshot, not PATH).

## Fix

- `runner/daemon.js` `detectAvailableHarnesses` now probes PATH + standard
  install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`) + per-harness install dirs
  (pi: `~/.pi/agent/bin`, `$PI_AGENT_DIR/bin`) + `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides,
  and pi additionally via its `models.json` snapshot — reusing
  `standardSearchDirs`/`piSnapshotPath`/`DISCOVERY_ENV_VARS` from
  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` so Runner and backend detect the same
  harnesses on the same host. `probeHarnessVersions` resolves binaries
  through the same dirs (pi now reports a real version, not "unknown").
- `startRunner.sh` `detect_harnesses` probes the same set at install time.
- server2 ops: env switched to `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=auto` (backup kept
  beside it), updated `runner/daemon.js` + `startRunner.sh` copied to the
  deployed bundle (md5-verified identical), `systemctl --user restart
  kainbain-runner-server2-alpha.service`.

# server2 auto-detect fix — verification record (2026-11-10)

## Root cause of the human-reported failure

server2's runner env (`~/.kainbain/runner-server2-alpha.env`) pinned
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=muse`, so the daemon's harness list was
`['muse']` and the discovery round only ran the muse leg — journal showed
`Model discovery: 0 model(s) (muse:0)` on every Re-detect, even with the
latest runner code deployed. On top of that, the Runner's harness
auto-detect probed only PATH, and server2's systemd PATH
(`/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`) does not include
`~/.local/bin` or `~/.pi/agent/bin`, so even `auto` would have missed pi
(the backend's own `discoverHarnesses` detects pi via the
`~/.pi/agent/models.json` snapshot, not PATH).

## Fix

- `runner/daemon.js` `detectAvailableHarnesses` now probes PATH + standard
  install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`) + per-harness install dirs
  (pi: `~/.pi/agent/bin`, `$PI_AGENT_DIR/bin`) + `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides,
  and pi additionally via its `models.json` snapshot — reusing
  `standardSearchDirs`/`piSnapshotPath`/`DISCOVERY_ENV_VARS` from
  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` so Runner and backend detect the same
  harnesses on the same host. `probeHarnessVersions` resolves binaries
  through the same dirs (pi now reports a real version, not "unknown").
- `startRunner.sh` `detect_harnesses` probes the same set at install time.
- server2 ops: env switched to `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=auto` (backup kept
  beside it), updated `runner/daemon.js` + `startRunner.sh` copied to the
  deployed bundle (md5-verified identical), `systemctl --user restart
  kainbain-runner-server2-alpha.service`.

# Implementation Plan — Runner auto-detect models from all supported harnesses

## Goal

Every Runner auto-detects the models of each harness it serves (not just
`muse`), advertises them to the backend through the existing heartbeat,
and the existing UI Refresh / Re-detect controls drive a fresh scan.
Concrete target: a host like server2 with `pi` configured must serve its
pi models into the fleet picker with no hand-typed model list.

## Context and evidence

- Runner discovery today is muse-only: `discoverClaudeModels()` in
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`muse serve` → `model/list`), and
  `refreshDiscoveredModels()` in `runner/daemon.js` returns early unless
  `muse` is in the configured harness list.
- The Runner bundle ships `runner/` + `api/` + `shared/` (see `deploy.sh`
  staging) and `startRunner.sh` runs `npm ci --prefix runner/api`, so the
  Runner host HAS the backend harness modules and their deps (including
  the pi SDK `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`). `defaultLoadHarness()`
  already imports backend harness factories on the Runner.
- Backend per-harness discovery already exists and is the behavior to
  reuse, not reimplement:
  - `pi`: `piHarness.listModels()` from `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()`
    (only providers with VALID credentials appear — matches survey q2).
  - `antigravity`: `agyModelCatalog.js` (`agy models` spawn + parse, TTL
    cache, classified `{code,message,hint}` errors).
  - `opencode`: `OpencodeModelDiscovery.js` (`/config/providers` fetch).
  - `muse`: MSP `model/list` (`museMspModelCatalog.js`; Runner leg exists).
  - `vibe`: ACP handshake model select (`vibeModelCatalog.js`); exec path
    honestly empty.
  - `codex`: theoretical shim, honestly empty (`listModels()` → `[]`).
  - `custom`/`mock`: no discovery (`none`, or test-only).
- Refresh plumbing already exists end to end and only needs generalizing:
  `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` "Re-detect models" →
  `api.requestModelRediscovery(runnerId)` → `RUNNER_COMMANDS` heartbeat
  pull channel (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, ADR 0013) →
  `handlePendingCommands()` → `refreshDiscoveredModels()` → ack
  `discovered N model(s)` → next heartbeat `facts.models` → fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog`) → picker fleet badges

# server2 auto-detect fix — verification record (2026-11-10)

## Root cause of the human-reported failure

server2's runner env (`~/.kainbain/runner-server2-alpha.env`) pinned
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=muse`, so the daemon's harness list was
`['muse']` and the discovery round only ran the muse leg — journal showed
`Model discovery: 0 model(s) (muse:0)` on every Re-detect, even with the
latest runner code deployed. On top of that, the Runner's harness
auto-detect probed only PATH, and server2's systemd PATH
(`/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`) does not include
`~/.local/bin` or `~/.pi/agent/bin`, so even `auto` would have missed pi
(the backend's own `discoverHarnesses` detects pi via the
`~/.pi/agent/models.json` snapshot, not PATH).

## Fix

- `runner/daemon.js` `detectAvailableHarnesses` now probes PATH + standard
  install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`) + per-harness install dirs
  (pi: `~/.pi/agent/bin`, `$PI_AGENT_DIR/bin`) + `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides,
  and pi additionally via its `models.json` snapshot — reusing
  `standardSearchDirs`/`piSnapshotPath`/`DISCOVERY_ENV_VARS` from
  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` so Runner and backend detect the same
  harnesses on the same host. `probeHarnessVersions` resolves binaries
  through the same dirs (pi now reports a real version, not "unknown").
- `startRunner.sh` `detect_harnesses` probes the same set at install time.
- server2 ops: env switched to `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=auto` (backup kept
  beside it), updated `runner/daemon.js` + `startRunner.sh` copied to the
  deployed bundle (md5-verified identical), `systemctl --user restart
  kainbain-runner-server2-alpha.service`.

# Implementation Plan — Runner auto-detect models from all supported harnesses

## Goal

Every Runner auto-detects the models of each harness it serves (not just
`muse`), advertises them to the backend through the existing heartbeat,
and the existing UI Refresh / Re-detect controls drive a fresh scan.
Concrete target: a host like server2 with `pi` configured must serve its
pi models into the fleet picker with no hand-typed model list.

## Context and evidence

- Runner discovery today is muse-only: `discoverClaudeModels()` in
  `runner/modelDiscovery.js` (`muse serve` → `model/list`), and
  `refreshDiscoveredModels()` in `runner/daemon.js` returns early unless
  `muse` is in the configured harness list.
- The Runner bundle ships `runner/` + `api/` + `shared/` (see `deploy.sh`
  staging) and `startRunner.sh` runs `npm ci --prefix runner/api`, so the
  Runner host HAS the backend harness modules and their deps (including
  the pi SDK `@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`). `defaultLoadHarness()`
  already imports backend harness factories on the Runner.
- Backend per-harness discovery already exists and is the behavior to
  reuse, not reimplement:
  - `pi`: `piHarness.listModels()` from `ModelRuntime.getAvailableSnapshot()`
    (only providers with VALID credentials appear — matches survey q2).
  - `antigravity`: `agyModelCatalog.js` (`agy models` spawn + parse, TTL
    cache, classified `{code,message,hint}` errors).
  - `opencode`: `OpencodeModelDiscovery.js` (`/config/providers` fetch).
  - `muse`: MSP `model/list` (`museMspModelCatalog.js`; Runner leg exists).
  - `vibe`: ACP handshake model select (`vibeModelCatalog.js`); exec path
    honestly empty.
  - `codex`: theoretical shim, honestly empty (`listModels()` → `[]`).
  - `custom`/`mock`: no discovery (`none`, or test-only).
- Refresh plumbing already exists end to end and only needs generalizing:
  `RunnerConfigurationSection.jsx` "Re-detect models" →
  `api.requestModelRediscovery(runnerId)` → `RUNNER_COMMANDS` heartbeat
  pull channel (`api/flow/runnerRegistry.js`, ADR 0013) →
  `handlePendingCommands()` → `refreshDiscoveredModels()` → ack
  `discovered N model(s)` → next heartbeat `facts.models` → fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog`) → picker fleet badges

# server2 auto-detect fix — verification record (2026-11-10)

## Root cause of the human-reported failure

server2's runner env (`~/.kainbain/runner-server2-alpha.env`) pinned
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=muse`, so the daemon's harness list was
`['muse']` and the discovery round only ran the muse leg — journal showed
`Model discovery: 0 model(s) (muse:0)` on every Re-detect, even with the
latest runner code deployed. On top of that, the Runner's harness
auto-detect probed only PATH, and server2's systemd PATH
(`/usr/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`) does not include
`~/.local/bin` or `~/.pi/agent/bin`, so even `auto` would have missed pi
(the backend's own `discoverHarnesses` detects pi via the
`~/.pi/agent/models.json` snapshot, not PATH).

## Fix

- `runner/daemon.js` `detectAvailableHarnesses` now probes PATH + standard
  install dirs (`~/.local/bin`, `~/bin`) + per-harness install dirs
  (pi: `~/.pi/agent/bin`, `$PI_AGENT_DIR/bin`) + `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides,
  and pi additionally via its `models.json` snapshot — reusing
  `standardSearchDirs`/`piSnapshotPath`/`DISCOVERY_ENV_VARS` from
  `api/agent/harnessDiscovery.js` so Runner and backend detect the same
  harnesses on the same host. `probeHarnessVersions` resolves binaries
  through the same dirs (pi now reports a real version, not "unknown").
- `startRunner.sh` `detect_harnesses` probes the same set at install time.
- server2 ops: env switched to `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=auto` (backup kept
  beside it), updated `runner/daemon.js` + `startRunner.sh` copied to the
  deployed bundle (md5-verified identical), `systemctl --user restart
  kainbain-runner-server2-alpha.service`.

# Harness registry & the model catalogue API

How the engine declares which agent harnesses exist, and how the UI's harness-first
model selector consumes that data.

## The seam

`api/agent/harnessRegistry.js` is the ONE place that knows **which harnesses exist** —
both as the construction + selection registry (factories, memoized instances,
per-project resolution: `project.harness` → `config.defaultHarness` → `"pi"`, with a
warn-once fallback for unknown names) and as the id-keyed HTTP VIEW registry
(`createHarnessRegistry()`) that `api/index.js` materializes once at startup and hands
to the `/harnesses` routes. Harness construction stays in `api/agent/harnesses/pi`, and
the session-behaviour contract stays in `harnessContract.js`. A future harness
registers a factory (`registerHarness("name", factory, { description })`) **and** is
projected into the composition root's view registry — every consumer below grows a
second entry without route or UI changes.

Model catalogues are a **harness contract capability**: each harness exposes
`listModels({ refresh })`, and every model view serves that listing projected onto the
stable public shape by `listPublicModels({ harness, refresh })` in `api/models.js`
(TTL-cached per harness id by the process-wide `modelListCache`, curated
`FALLBACK_MODELS` when a harness yields nothing/fails, `publicModelJsonSchema`
validation, harness-scoped `key` tagging — see `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md`).

## `GET /compute/models` response

```json
{
  "models": [{ "key": "pi::google::gemini-2.5-pro", "harness": "pi", "id": "…", "name": "…", "provider": "…", "input": ["text"] }],
  "harnesses": [
    { "id": "pi", "label": "pi coding agent", "description": "pi-backed AgentHarness …", "models": [ …same objects… ] }
  ]
}
```

- `models` is the default harness's catalogue (`sessionStore.getHarness()` through
  `getAvailableModels({ refresh, harness })` in `api/routes/compute.js`) — the flat
  view sessions actually resolve against.
- `harnesses` is **additive** and built by `harnessesView()` (routes/compute.js) from
  `deps.harnessRegistry.list()`: each entry carries the registry entry's `id`, its
  display `name` as `label`, its `description`, and its own catalogue through the same
  `listModels()` source. The default harness's entry reuses the flat `models` array (one
  cache slot, one listing) so `harnesses[0].models` is always the exact flat catalogue.
  The field must stay declared in the route's response schema — Fastify strips response
  fields missing from the schema.
- `?refresh=true` bypasses the model cache for both views (network-free disk refresh).
- The same data is also served per harness by `/harnesses` (identity + capabilities +
  live `isDefault`) and `/harnesses/:id/models` (one harness's catalogue).

## Frontend consumption

- `frontend/src/services/api.js` — `fetchCachedModels` caches the whole body (client TTL
  60 s, in-flight sharing) and normalizes a missing `harnesses` to `[]` (older backend /
  mocked doubles); `groupModelsByProvider(models)` turns a flat list into
  `SelectDropdown` options grouped by provider (providers in first-appearance order,
  provider-less models in an `Ungrouped` bucket); `modelOptionValue` prefers the
  backend's harness-scoped `key`.
- `frontend/src/hooks/useModelCatalog.js` — single fetch point returning
  `{ models, harnesses, loading }` with the app-wide fallback semantics.
- `frontend/src/components/common/ModelSelector.jsx` — the harness-first picker
  (see `docs/UI/DESIGN_SPEC.md` §3.6). It renders the harness row above the grouped
  model list; with no `harnesses` from the backend it wraps the flat catalogue as the
  single `pi` row, so the harness-first layout never collapses.

## Stored selection format

`project.defaultModel` and `stage.model` keep the shared reference grammar: canonical
`harness::provider::id` keys (what the current backend serves as `key` and the selector
emits on change), legacy `provider::id` composites, and oldest bare ids/names — every
resolver accepts all three, so nothing already stored breaks
(`docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md` has the grammar and resolution order). The harness
choice in the selector is UI navigation, not persisted state; server-side resolution
(`agentRunner` → harness `resolveModelRef`) hands the dispatch-resolved ref to session
creation (target hand-off, ADR 0005), so a cross-harness run never re-resolves the
project default against the wrong catalogue.

## Target hand-off & save-time validation tiers

Dispatch owns the harness+model combination for stage runs: `agentRunner` forwards
`stageMeta.model` alongside `stageMeta.harness`, the session store threads it into
`harness.createSession`, and the harness pins it (skipping `resolveInitialModel`).
`none`-selection harnesses accept and ignore the hand-off. The session-init log line
reports the resolved pair (one peeked display-target read, no rotation consumed).

Project saves validate stored combinations in two tiers (`api/aliasTargets.js`, wired
in `POST/PATCH /projects`):

- **Hard (400):** model on a `none` harness; unknown harness id; malformed ref.
- **Soft (200 + `warnings[]`):** catalog-miss targets/defaults; ignored defaults on
  `none` harnesses; unresolvable project-default aliases.

Response-schema note: any added `warnings` field on save responses must be declared
in the Fastify response schema or Fastify strips it — the POST 201 schema declares
`warnings: string[]` (PATCH carries no response schema, so it passes through). The
Settings UI surfaces `warnings[]` inline next to the save button, badges each alias
target (`valid` / `unknown-model` / `unknown-harness`), and warns — with explicit
"Pick a model for this harness" / "Keep and warn" actions, never an auto-rewrite —
when the stored default no longer resolves in the effective harness's catalogue.

**Follow-up:** when a second harness is registered, the additive `harnesses[]` view and
the selector already support it (the model list simply switches with the harness row);
persisting the harness choice per project/stage stays an explicit follow-up until then.

## Runner-side auto-detect (fleet catalogue source)

Runners advertise the same harness-scoped keys into the fleet catalogue
(`buildFleetModelCatalog` over heartbeat `facts.models`): one discovery leg
per configured harness in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` (the harness
list itself comes from auto-detect — PATH plus `~/.local/bin`/`~/bin`,
per-harness install dirs, `KAINBAIN_*_BIN` overrides, and pi's
`~/.pi/agent` snapshot — see `runner/daemon.js` `detectAvailableHarnesses`,
mirroring the backend's `discoverHarnesses`), each reusing
its backend harness's own `listModels()` as the single source of truth for
"ready to use right now" (survey q2). The Runner's
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS`/`MODEL` pin wins over auto-detect by default
(pinned installs skip scanning; survey q4 discovery-wins is opt-in via
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1`);
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS=0` disables scanning; a failed
or empty scan keeps the previous list per harness (survey q5). The
Re-detect button in Settings › Runners drives `requestModelRediscovery`
over the heartbeat pull channel (survey q3) and the ack
(`discovered N model(s) (pi:12, muse:3)`) plus the heartbeat
`facts.discoveryStatus` (`{ [harness]: { ok, count, atMs, error? } }`)
surface per-harness counts and the first leg warning. Empty scans fail
loud, never silent: pi reports `PI_MODELS_EMPTY` (with the login state),
muse reports `MUSE_MSP_BIN_MISSING` / `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY`, and a round
that sees detected-but-unconfigured harnesses appends the
`harness auto-detect also sees: …` hint (re-detection scans configured
harnesses only). Detected models join
the picker as normal fleet choices (survey q6) — see `runner/README.md`
for the per-harness legs matrix.

projected into the composition root's view registry — every consumer below grows a
second entry without route or UI changes.

`listModels({ refresh })`, and every model view serves that listing projected onto the
stable public shape by `listPublicModels({ harness, refresh })` in `api/models.js`

```json
  ]
```

# Runner daemon (`runner/`)

Out-of-process task executor — the ONLY way agent stages run (runner-only).
Implements ADR 0009 steps 1–6 over the HTTP wire protocol — no engine,
session, or store access. The assignment is explicit config by default;
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_DISPATCH=1` switches to the capability-aware dispatch
loop (WP-3.1), where the backend picks each task.

Local and remote Runners run the identical binary and protocol. The only
difference is environment: a local Runner points at
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_BACKEND=http://localhost:3100`, a remote Runner at the
backend URL (e.g. `https://kainbain.home`). Every host ships one local
Runner by default — install it with:

```sh
scripts/install-local-runner.sh --id local-pi
# remote host: add --backend https://kainbain.home
# Harnesses auto-detect by default (pi, muse, antigravity, vibe probed on
# PATH plus the standard install dirs ~/.local/bin and ~/bin, each harness's
# own install dir, and pi additionally via its ~/.pi/agent models.json
# snapshot — so SDK-only pi installs that are not on the service PATH are
# still detected); pin with --manual --harness pi or
# --manual --harnesses pi,muse. mock has no CLI, so it is manual-only.
```

## Onboard (human approval required, D4)

1. Set the join secret on the backend (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN`) and
   approve the Runner in Settings › Harness › Runners (or
   `POST /runners/:id/approve`).
2. Start the daemon with the one-time credential shown once in the UI:

```sh
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_BACKEND=http://localhost:3100 \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN=[REDACTED]] secret> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_CREDENTIAL=[REDACTED]] credential from Settings> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_ID=host-1 \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=mock \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECT_ID=<projectId> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_TASK_ID=<taskId> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT=/var/lib/kainbain/runner-work \
node runner/main.js
```

Without `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_CREDENTIAL` the daemon registers, polls until the
join is approved, then exits telling you to paste the credential. It never
fetches the credential back over the wire.

## Dispatch loop (WP-3.1)

```sh
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_BACKEND=http://localhost:3100 \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_JOIN_TOKEN=[REDACTED]] secret> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_CREDENTIAL=[REDACTED]] credential from Settings> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_ID=host-1 \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=mock \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS=<csv this host can serve, optional> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_DISPATCH=1 \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECTS=<projectId,optional allowlist> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_DISPATCH_POLL_MS=5000 \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_DISPATCH_IDLE_LIMIT=3 \
node runner/main.js
```

`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODELS` is the servable-model advertisement the backend
matches against (csv; singular `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL` seeds a
1-element pin; empty matches model-less tasks only). A pinned list
always wins over discovered ids: pinned installs skip discovery scans
(boot, cadence, and Re-detect all ack `models pinned; discovery
skipped`) and keep advertising exactly their pin across self-updates.
Set `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1` to opt in to
discovery-wins (survey q4: a non-empty discovery result replaces the
pin, the pin only fills in while discovery yielded nothing). Each
assignment serves exactly the dispatch answer's required model — never
a substitution.

The daemon auto-discovers models with one leg per configured harness
(`runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js`), each reusing its backend
harness's own `listModels()` so "ready to use" means the same thing on
both sides (box-local login — keys never leave the host). Only models
ready right now are listed; ids advertise in the fleet grammar
`<harness>::<provider>::<model>`:

| Harness | Source | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `pi` | pi SDK availability snapshot | Needs `~/.pi/agent` login; empty login reports `PI_MODELS_EMPTY` (login state in the message) |
| `muse` | `muse serve` stdio `model/list` | Needs the `muse` CLI (resolved off-PATH too); missing CLI = `MUSE_MSP_BIN_MISSING`, zero-row answer = `MUSE_MSP_MODELS_EMPTY` |
| `antigravity` | `agy models` spawn + parse | Classified `{code,message,hint}` errors |
| `vibe` | ACP handshake model select | Exec-only hosts list nothing (honest empty + retained error) |
| `opencode` | `GET {OPENCODE_URL}/config/providers` | Needs `OPENCODE_URL` (+ `OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD`); unset = honest empty + `OPENCODE_NOT_CONFIGURED` |

   `POST /runners/:id/approve`).
2. Start the daemon with the one-time credential shown once in the UI:

```sh

KAINBAIN_RUNNER_CREDENTIAL=[REDACTED]]] credential from Settings> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_ID=host-1 \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_HARNESS=mock \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_PROJECT_ID=<projectId> \
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_TASK_ID=<taskId> \
```

name: server2-ssh
description: Access the second server at 192.168.1.172 as user server2 over SSH using the password file without exposing it.
---

# Server2 SSH

Connect to the second server (`server2@192.168.1.172`) and run commands or copy files. The password is stored in `~/.passwrd`.

Connection details:

- Host: `192.168.1.172`
- User: `server2`
- Password file: `~/.passwrd` (mode `600`, first line is the password)

## When to use

- User asks to access, check, or run something on `server2`, the second server, or `192.168.1.172`.
- Any `server2@192.168.1.172` SSH, SCP, or SFTP task.

## Security rules (must follow)

- NEVER display the password: do not `cat`, `read`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `echo`, `print`, `base64`, `od`, `hexdump`, or open `~/.passwrd` in an editor or pager.
- NEVER put the password on a command line or in an environment variable via substitution such as `$(cat ~/.passwrd)`, backticks, `xargs`, or `export PASS=...`.
- NEVER use `sshpass -p`, `sshpass --password`, or type the password interactively where it can be logged.
- Only use tools that consume the password file directly so the secret never enters model output:
  - `sshpass -f ~/.passwrd ...`
  - or the Python `pexpect` fallback below, which opens `~/.passwrd` internally and never prints it.
- Keep `~/.passwrd` at mode `600`. Check with `ls -l ~/.passwrd` (do not read it).

## Prerequisite

`sshpass` reads the file with `-f` without exposing it:

```bash
command -v sshpass || echo "missing"
```

If missing, install it (requires sudo):

```bash
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y sshpass
```

If `sudo`/install is not possible, use the Python fallback below (`pexpect` ships with the system Python).

## Method 1: sshpass (preferred)

Run a remote command:

```bash
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new server2@192.168.1.172 'echo ok; hostname; whoami'
```

Interactive shell:

```bash
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new server2@192.168.1.172
```

Copy files:

```bash
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new file.txt server2@192.168.1.172:~/
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -r server2@192.168.1.172:/remote/path/ ./local-path/
```

Keep the `-f ~/.passwrd` form. Do not replace it with `-p` or with shell substitution.

## Method 2: Python fallback (no sudo needed)

Use when `sshpass` is not installed. This snippet opens `~/.passwrd` inside Python and drives the password prompt. It never prints the password:

```bash
python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
import pathlib, sys, pexpect
pwd = [REDACTED]().joinpath(".passwrd").read_text().splitlines()[0].strip()
remote_cmd = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]) or "echo ok; hostname; whoami"
child = pexpect.spawn(
    f"ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new server2@192.168.1.172 {remote_cmd!r}",
    encoding="utf-8", timeout=20,
)
i = child.expect(["[Pp]assword:", pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
if i == 0:
    child.sendline(pwd)
    child.expect([pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
print(child.before)
PY
```

Pass the remote command as arguments after `--`, for example `python3 - "uptime"`.

## Troubleshooting

- `Permission denied (publickey,password)`: the password file or account changed; verify `ls -l ~/.passwrd` exists and retry one command. Do not dump the file to debug.
- `Connection timed out` / `No route to host`: check `ping -c1 192.168.1.172` and that both machines are on the same LAN.
- `sshpass: command not found`: install it or use Method 2.
- `Host key verification failed`: use `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` once on a trusted LAN, then keep the default.

# Server2 SSH

Connect to the second server (`server2@192.168.1.172`) and run commands or copy files. The password is stored in `~/.passwrd`.

Connection details:

- Host: `192.168.1.172`
- User: `server2`
- Password file: `~/.passwrd` (mode `600`, first line is the password)

## When to use

- User asks to access, check, or run something on `server2`, the second server, or `192.168.1.172`.
- Any `server2@192.168.1.172` SSH, SCP, or SFTP task.

## Security rules (must follow)

- NEVER display the password: do not `cat`, `read`, `head`, `tail`, `less`, `echo`, `print`, `base64`, `od`, `hexdump`, or open `~/.passwrd` in an editor or pager.
- NEVER put the password on a command line or in an environment variable via substitution such as `$(cat ~/.passwrd)`, backticks, `xargs`, or `export PASS=...`.
- NEVER use `sshpass -p`, `sshpass --password`, or type the password interactively where it can be logged.
- Only use tools that consume the password file directly so the secret never enters model output:
  - `sshpass -f ~/.passwrd ...`
  - or the Python `pexpect` fallback below, which opens `~/.passwrd` internally and never prints it.
- Keep `~/.passwrd` at mode `600`. Check with `ls -l ~/.passwrd` (do not read it).

## Prerequisite

`sshpass` reads the file with `-f` without exposing it:

```bash
command -v sshpass || echo "missing"
```

If missing, install it (requires sudo):

```bash
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y sshpass
```

If `sudo`/install is not possible, use the Python fallback below (`pexpect` ships with the system Python).

## Method 1: sshpass (preferred)

Run a remote command:

```bash
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new server2@192.168.1.172 'echo ok; hostname; whoami'
```

Interactive shell:

```bash
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new server2@192.168.1.172
```

Copy files:

```bash
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new file.txt server2@192.168.1.172:~/
sshpass -f ~/.passwrd scp -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -r server2@192.168.1.172:/remote/path/ ./local-path/
```

Keep the `-f ~/.passwrd` form. Do not replace it with `-p` or with shell substitution.

## Method 2: Python fallback (no sudo needed)

Use when `sshpass` is not installed. This snippet opens `~/.passwrd` inside Python and drives the password prompt. It never prints the password:

```bash
python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
import pathlib, sys, pexpect
pwd = [REDACTED]().joinpath(".passwrd").read_text().splitlines()[0].strip()
remote_cmd = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]) or "echo ok; hostname; whoami"
child = pexpect.spawn(
    f"ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new server2@192.168.1.172 {remote_cmd!r}",
    encoding="utf-8", timeout=20,
)
i = child.expect(["[Pp]assword:", pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
if i == 0:
    child.sendline(pwd)
    child.expect([pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
print(child.before)
PY
```

Pass the remote command as arguments after `--`, for example `python3 - "uptime"`.

## Troubleshooting

- `Permission denied (publickey,password)`: the password file or account changed; verify `ls -l ~/.passwrd` exists and retry one command. Do not dump the file to debug.
- `Connection timed out` / `No route to host`: check `ping -c1 192.168.1.172` and that both machines are on the same LAN.
- `sshpass: command not found`: install it or use Method 2.
- `Host key verification failed`: use `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new` once on a trusted LAN, then keep the default.
